Summarizing bird migration and stopovers within urbanized landscapes using Motus data

Author

Steffi LaZerte

Published

July 4, 2024

Pilot Phase

Principal Investigators: Barbara Frei, Elizabeth Gow and Krista De Groot
Workflow design: Steffi LaZerte

Getting Started

This site contains the workflow for obtaining and filtering Motus track data for the analysis of Urban/Rural stopovers during avian migration.

This website contains the full annotated code and outputs run as of the dates on each page.

There are two ways to use this workflow

  1. Walk through this website, familiarize yourself with the code and outputs [Most users]

  2. Modify this workflow by working directly in the qmd scripts used to create this workflow [Some users]

    • To do this, you can either create a PR to the workflow or clone it and work on your own copy.
    • Each qmd file is setup to be run interactively (i.e. in an R session) as well as to be compiled non-interactively to create this script
    • Be warned that compiling the whole site can take a long time, especially if new data is being downloaded!
    • Use renv::restore() to ensure you have the same packages and versions installed in this project to reproduce this workflow.

Packages and Reproducibility

All R packages used in this workflow are loaded by the XX_setup.R (see the Appendix Setup).

We use renv to keep track of the packages used and their versions. Use renv::restore() to double check that your version of this project has the correct packages ready to go. If all goes as planned renv should install the packages for you if you’re missing any.

Each script ends with a “Reproducibility” block which includes the session information with specific packages used when that page was last compiled.

For publication, check the Citations Appendix to ensure we use proper citations.

Understanding outputs

Each page performs a different step in the workflow (in order), from downloading the data, to filtering, to summarizing.
